questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A crucial aspect in choosing my study destination was finding a university that offered a good study program closely aligned with my academic interests and career goals. I wanted a program that combined strong theoretical foundations with practical applications, providing both academic depth and relevant skills for the job market

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The process was a bit confusing and felt somewhat unstructured. It took some time to figure out where to find the necessary information, as there wasn’t a clear overview or central source for new arrivals.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing really. There wasn’t much direct assistance offered upon arrival, so I had to manage most things on my own and figure them out gradually.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really easy to find off-campus housing. There were plenty of available options online, and the process was straightforward and quick. I’d recommend starting the search early just to get the best location and price.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It’s a great opportunity to meet people from other universities or study programs and to experience more of the local community. Living off campus also gives you more independence and flexibility in your daily life.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was quite straightforward. I mainly had to get a document signed and approved by the university, which confirmed my course selections. Overall, the process was simple but not very detailed in terms of guidance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a career center where I think you could ask questions or get some assistance with academic or administrative matters. However, I didn’t make much use of it myself.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all the classes I wanted without any major issues. The process went smoothly once the registration opened.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to pick the classes you’re genuinely interested in and confirm that they fit your schedule early on. It’s a good idea to double-check course requirements and get everything signed as soon as possible to avoid last-minute issues.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a mix of courses, including three at the master’s level and three at the bachelor’s level. The master’s courses were more research-oriented and required deeper analytical work, while the bachelor’s courses focused more on foundational theory and practical applications. Overall, the workload was balanced but slightly more demanding than expected.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more interactive, with a stronger focus on class engagement and student participation. There were also more presentations and group discussions compared to UCPH, which made the classes feel more dynamic and collaborative.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Economic Growth
Neuroeconomics
Industrial Organisation
International Business
International Management

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking International Business and International Management. Both courses were taught by very knowledgeable professors who encouraged active participation and critical thinking. There were also plenty of class debates and discussions, which made the learning experience more engaging and helped develop a global perspective on business-related topics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Traveling around turned out to be more expensive than I expected. While local transportation was affordable, longer trips and weekend getaways added up quickly, especially when factoring in accommodation and activities.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and public transport were both less expensive than I expected. Groceries and meals at local places were quite affordable, and public transportation was reliable and reasonably priced compared to what I’m used to.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much same selection as UCPH

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played tennis during my exchange, which was a great way to stay active and meet new people. However, I’d recommend that future students choose activities that match their own interests — whether it’s sports, student clubs, or local events — since it’s one of the best ways to connect with others and experience the local culture.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I’d definitely recommend traveling around the Netherlands. The country is easy to explore by train, and there are so many charming cities and cultural spots to visit. Places like Utrecht, Rotterdam, and The Hague are all worth seeing, and weekend trips give a great sense of the local culture.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy to adjust. People were friendly, open-minded, and spoke excellent English, which made daily life and communication very smooth. I felt welcome from the beginning.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be yourself and stay open to meeting new people. I found everyone I met to be kind, polite, and easy to talk to. Joining group activities or student events is also a great way to connect with local students naturally.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Dutch can be quite reserved at first, which sometimes made it a bit challenging to get to know people right away. However, once you start talking to them, they are friendly and direct, which I came to really appreciate.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the food and the overall lifestyle. People seemed to value balance and enjoy a relaxed pace of life, with time for socializing, outdoor activities, and good meals.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Have fun and make the most of your time abroad.
2. Don’t be afraid to reach out and talk to new people — everyone is open and welcoming once you start a conversation.
3. Take time to travel around and experience different parts of the Netherlands; it’s an easy and rewarding way to explore the country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rent a bike on the very first day. It makes getting around so much easier and helps you feel like part of the local culture right away. Biking is the main mode of transportation, and it’s both convenient and fun.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made were definitely the most rewarding part. Meeting people from different backgrounds and cultures gave me new perspectives and made the whole experience much more meaningful.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was participating in debates and public speaking in a foreign language. It took some time to build confidence, but it was also a valuable learning experience that helped improve my communication skills.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
